title: Whiteboard Package Workflow Map
description: Interactive documentation of how frontend components, hooks, state modules, recognition clients, and backend packages collaborate during whiteboard actions.

nodes.label: App
nodes.summary: Top-level composition point. Owns shell state, wires callbacks, holds engineRef, tracks audit status, and passes flow state into UI components.

nodes.label: Toolbar
nodes.summary: Drawing control surface for tool selection, pen color, brush size, undo, redo, and clear.

nodes.label: ModelShell
nodes.summary: Right-side response and debug panel. Emits Submit and Next Problem actions and displays recognition, audit, and grading details.

nodes.label: LatexEquationDialog
nodes.summary: Custom problem entry surface shown when the flow is waiting for an equation.

nodes.label: WhiteboardStage
nodes.summary: Canvas host that creates CanvasStrokeEngine, forwards viewport/tool updates, and renders the problem overlay.

nodes.label: ProblemLayer
nodes.summary: DOM overlay for problem prompts, answer boxes, submitted boxes, and debug rectangles.

nodes.label: useProblemFlowController
nodes.summary: Main orchestration hook. Owns problemFlow, scheduler lifecycle, recognition updates, grading bootstrap, submit, next, and custom problem actions.

nodes.label: useViewportController
nodes.summary: Owns current viewport, reset visibility, home movement, and animated viewport transitions.

nodes.label: useToolbarCollapse
nodes.summary: Controls active drawing tool and automatic toolbar collapse while drawing.

nodes.label: useWhiteboardShortcuts
nodes.summary: Keyboard shortcut bridge for tool changes and debug box toggling.

nodes.label: useE2ETestBridge
nodes.summary: Test-only browser bridge for pausing recognition, inspecting app state, and collecting recorded events.

nodes.label: problemFlow state
nodes.summary: Pure state module for problem sessions, answer boxes, submission state, recognition progress, next-problem positioning, and custom problem creation.

nodes.label: equationProblemSource
nodes.summary: Optional E2E problem source loader for dynamic problem catalogs.

nodes.label: CanvasStrokeEngine
nodes.summary: Pointer, drawing, panning, erasing, history, and callback engine for the foreground/background canvases.

nodes.label: StrokeStore
nodes.summary: Mutable stroke collection and history backing undo, redo, clear, and stroke reads.

nodes.label: CanvasRenderer
nodes.summary: Canvas drawing and redraw routines for persisted strokes and active stroke previews.

nodes.label: StrokeSmoother
nodes.summary: Normalizes and smooths pointer samples into renderable whiteboard strokes.

nodes.label: viewport + geometry + constants
nodes.summary: Shared board geometry, bounding-box helpers, viewport math, board size, and styling constants.

nodes.label: IncrementalRecognitionScheduler
nodes.summary: Debounced recognition coordinator. Tracks input signatures, segments strokes, runs line/full-answer recognition, emits snapshots, and aborts stale runs.

nodes.label: lineSegmentation
nodes.summary: Builds candidate math lines from answer strokes, boxes, overlaps, detections, and problem context.

nodes.label: studentWritingPipeline
nodes.summary: Full recognition pipeline: detection, segmentation, rasterization, OCR, semantic scoring, grading, candidate selection, retries, and final lines.

nodes.label: lineRasterizer
nodes.summary: Converts stroke candidates into line image data URLs for OCR.

nodes.label: OCR + segmentation clients
nodes.summary: Browser fetch clients for /recognize and /segment-lines via the local recognition API.

nodes.label: semanticClient
nodes.summary: Browser fetch client for /score-latex-candidates.

nodes.label: auditClient
nodes.summary: Decides when recognition needs VLM audit, compacts payloads, enqueues audit jobs, and polls audit status.

nodes.label: gradingClient
nodes.summary: Browser fetch client for /grade-math-work and /grade-equation-work.

nodes.label: FastAPI app
nodes.summary: Creates the recognition API, CORS middleware, scorer wiring, audit service, and route registration.

nodes.label: recognition routes
nodes.summary: Proxies /recognize, /segment-lines, and upstream /health to the configured CoMER/DBNet service.

nodes.label: grading routes
nodes.summary: Runs semantic scoring and Python grading with timeouts for /score-latex-candidates, /grade-equation-work, and /grade-math-work.

nodes.label: Python grading
nodes.summary: Equation and answer grading implementation used by the FastAPI scoring routes.

nodes.label: audit routes + service
nodes.summary: Accepts audit jobs, calls/stores VLM audit work, and exposes audit job status.

nodes.label: health route
nodes.summary: Local server health endpoint.

nodes.label: styles
nodes.summary: CSS for shell layout, toolbar, model panel, and whiteboard surfaces.

nodes.label: E2E + testing
nodes.summary: Playwright flows, mocked recognition helpers, live recognition matrix, and Python/Node test coverage.

flows.label: Submit Answer
flows.summary: Freezes the active problem, marks it submitted, flushes any pending recognition, and lets recognition/audit updates continue into the debug panel.

steps.note: Submit is enabled only while the active problem is solving.
App records an E2E submit-answer event before delegating.
The controller reads the latest engine strokes for event details.
Pure state update sets status=submitted, freezes the answer box, and updates recognition status.
React re-renders problem overlays and shell button state.
Pending recognition is forced immediately instead of waiting for debounce.
The final answer pass produces selected lines, LaTeX, semantic data, and grading.
Snapshots are accepted for solving/submitted problems and merged into problem state.
Audits are triggered for grading misses, OCR failures, low confidence, conflicts, or sampling.
The backend accepts the job and later exposes status by auditId.
The shell displays submitted status, recognition output, grading, and audit state.

flows.label: Next Problem
flows.summary: Creates or selects the next problem session, moves the viewport to the new board position, and updates the prompt and answer region.

steps.note: The button is enabled only when the active problem is ready for next.
App delegates directly to the controller.
State decides whether to append a problem, finish the catalog, or await custom equation entry.
The next problem is placed below the frozen answer with a fixed gap.
The board animates so the new problem lands in the working area.
The active problem id, completed count, and awaitingEquation state drive the next render.
The stage receives updated problem geometry and viewport.
The new prompt and answer catchment appear on the board.
The shell updates the displayed equation and action availability.
Recognition is reattached to the new active solving problem.

flows.label: Write Stroke
flows.trigger: Pointer input on the whiteboard canvas
flows.summary: Captures pen movement, stores strokes, updates answer-box geometry, and starts the debounced recognition pipeline.

steps.note: The stage owns the canvases; the engine handles low-level drawing and gestures.
Raw pointer samples become a stable stroke shape.
The store keeps the stroke list and history.
The visible canvas updates immediately.
App records E2E events and collapses the toolbar while drawing.
Toolbar state reacts to active pen input.
The controller stores latest strokes and reconciles them with the active problem.
Answer stroke ids, content bbox, and active answer box are recalculated.
The scheduler builds a new input signature and schedules a debounced flush.
Candidate line groups are created for recognition.
A final/full-answer recognition pass selects the best line sequence.
Each candidate becomes image data for OCR.
OCR requests are sent through the local API.
FastAPI proxies OCR to the configured upstream model service.
Semantic scores help select the best candidate line cover.
The backend runs the configured semantic scorer with a timeout.
Grading evidence boosts final candidate selection and debug status.
Python grading returns solution coverage, classifications, and problem status.
The equation/answer grader classifies the student's work.
The controller merges recognition progress into problem state.
Debug mode exposes candidates, lines, grading, and audit state.

flows.label: Create Custom Problem
flows.summary: Turns user-entered LaTeX into a new problem session, places it on the board, and connects recognition to it.

steps.note: The dialog is mounted only while problemFlow.awaitingEquation is true.
The controller delegates validation and session creation to pure state.
A user-latex problem definition is created with problem metadata.
The custom problem is placed at the initial position or below the previous submitted problem.
The viewport moves to the new problem when needed.
awaitingEquation becomes false and activeProblemId points at the new session.
The custom equation appears on the board.
The shell shows the new problem and enables solving actions.
Recognition is now attached to the custom problem.

flows.label: Recognition Audit
flows.summary: Compacts recognition evidence, decides whether VLM review is needed, queues the audit, polls status, and shows the result in debug mode.

steps.note: Only new completed signatures are considered for audit.
Hard triggers include failed grading, unread lines, OCR failures, low confidence, and candidate conflicts.
The payload strips bulky image data and records previous audit id when available.
The API returns an audit id with HTTP 202.
The service writes/logs audit work according to server settings.
Status polling updates queued, processing, logged, disabled, or error state.
App stores audit status by problem id.
The debug panel shows whether audit was queued, logged, skipped, or failed.

flows.label: Initial Grading
flows.summary: Generates a baseline grading/solution payload for a problem before the student writes an answer.

steps.note: The effect runs once per problem id.
This is a non-blocking solution-generation call.
The server calls the configured math grading scorer.
The grader returns solution-set metadata and problem-level status.
The active problem stores baseline grading details when the call succeeds.
The shell can show richer status/debug information from the precomputed grading.
